applicableEnvironmentsNote: Flight packages declare their host environment as `flight.environment` in their own package.json -- web, electron, tauri, capacitor, node. A package whose declared environment is not listed here cannot apply to this profile, is reported as not-applicable, and is excluded from the shippable denominator. flight-cpp targets a native SDL host, which is not one of Flight's declared environments, so the list is EMPTY and exactly the environment-agnostic packages are applicable. This is derived from the pinned source on every run rather than enumerated here, so a package that gains or loses the declaration is reclassified without anyone editing this file.
note: Packages this profile does not hold to the compile gate, with the REASON distinguished by `kind`. `not-applicable` means the profile cannot provide the capability the package exists to implement -- a Canvas 2D renderer has no meaning on a host with no canvas -- so the package is not broken and is not counted in the shippable denominator. `defect` means the package should work here and does not; it stays in the denominator and is a debt. Neither kind is a silent skip: every gate that honors this file reports what it deferred, and a deferral is REFUSED when a non-deferred header includes the deferred package, because deferring something still reachable hides a real break instead of parking an irrelevant one. Deferral changes no generated output -- headers are still emitted and still compiled, so progress stays visible and un-deferring is a one-line change.
